methodology.order: Five unthrottled and five page-CDP-throttled, service-worker-blocked fresh contexts, alternating sequentially; then an independently instrumented diagnostic and one normal worker-enabled cold and warm reload.
methodology.pageThrottle: Only service-worker-blocked profile: CDP 100 ms latency, 500000 bytes/s down, 125000 bytes/s up, no CPU throttle. The worker-enabled visit has no emulation because page CDP does not globally throttle worker requests.
methodology.cache: Fresh browser context and CDP browser cache disabled for cold samples; service worker blocked. CDN edge cache, DNS, connection and network conditions may vary. SW-enabled cold starts with fresh context; warm replay reuses it.
methodology.ready: Wall time from page.goto to the observed Game ready flag. Diagnostic-only progress/draw hooks and response-byte capture are excluded from these formal timings.
methodology.provenance: Before and after each visit, a separate curl process reads cache-busted build-info.json. The Game's requested GLB paths and decoded lengths are checked against the pinned production game-pack manifest; the separate diagnostic also hashes actual consumed bytes.
limitations: Browser emulation and a headless desktop are not a physical mobile device.
Only the worker-enabled real-network journey can observe worker requests; page-target CDP throttling is not a global worker network throttle.
CDN edge caching, real network and external host workloads are not controlled.
Service-worker warm replay here does not prepare the optional offline Game pack.
Diagnostic hooks record the first draw call after final model progress, not GPU completion.
